Source format: Project Proposal Document

The residency is organized around four primary objectives:

1. **Material Investigation:** To systematically test the optical behaviour of low-wattage LED projectors when directed through a range of diffusing materials (including frosted acrylic, woven polypropylene, and recycled paper pulp) under controlled ambient light conditions.
2. **Spatial Calibration:** To develop a repeatable methodology for mapping light projection zones within a 200-square-metre rectangular gallery space, accounting for ceiling height, wall reflectance, and floor surface variations.
3. **Public Engagement:** To conduct six weekend workshops for undergraduate students and the general public, during which participants will co-build small-scale light sculptures using the project's material library.
4. **Knowledge Dissemination:** To produce a technical white paper and a curated photographic archive documenting the project's processes, failures, and findings for use by peer institutions.

**4. Artistic Vision and Conceptual Framework**

Lumen Atelier operates from the premise that projected light, when treated as a sculptural material rather than a mere illuminant, can alter the perceived depth and weight of architectural surfaces. Our working methodology draws on the traditions of the Light and Space movement of the 1960s, but updates this lineage through the use of affordable, digitally controlled projection hardware. Rather than aiming for spectacle, the project seeks a quiet, almost forensic examination of how light falls, bends, and dissolves across everyday building materials.

The Black Box Gallery (BBG-2) presents a particularly interesting challenge: its walls are clad in a dark, low-reflectance microfibre fabric that absorbs most ambient light. This makes the space ideal for projection work but also means that our material tests must account for unusually high contrast ratios. We intend to treat this constraint as a generative condition, not a limitation.

**5. Research Methodology**

In the project proposal document, the Lumen Atelier project phase is listed as proposal. Record status: historical.

The project will proceed through three overlapping research streams:

- **Stream A – Material Testing (October – December 2024):** Systematic testing of 15 diffusing materials across 5 projector models. Each test will record lux readings at 12 fixed grid points, photographic documentation of light falloff, and qualitative notes on perceived texture. Data will be logged in a shared spreadsheet and a physical sample book.
- **Stream B – Spatial Prototyping (January – April 2025):** Construction of three full-scale prototype installations within BBG-2, each occupying a different zone of the gallery. Prototypes will be open for informal viewing by faculty and students, with visitor feedback collected via a simple comment card system.
- **Stream C – Public Workshops and Exhibition (May – September 2025):** Delivery of six workshops and the final exhibition, titled "Lumen Atelier: Provisional Findings." The exhibition will present the three prototypes in their final form, alongside the material sample book and a looped video documentation of the testing process.

**6. Proposed Timeline**

| Period | Activity | Milestone |
|--------|----------|-----------|
| Oct – Nov 2024 | Procurement of equipment and materials; calibration of testing protocol | Equipment inventory approved |
| Dec 2024 – Feb 2025 | Stream A: Material testing and data collection | Interim data report (internal) |
| Mar – Apr 2025 | Stream B: Prototype construction and informal viewing | Three prototypes installed |
| May 2025 | Workshop series begins (six sessions over six weekends) | First workshop delivered |
| Jun – Jul 2025 | Refinement of prototypes based on feedback; documentation of process | Documentation draft complete |
| Aug 2025 | Final exhibition installation | Exhibition opens |
| Sep 2025 | Exhibition closes; white paper drafting and submission of final report | Final report to ORA |

**7. Project Team**
**8. Methodology**

The project adopts a practice-based research methodology, combining quantitative photometric measurement with qualitative spatial observation. The approach is informed by precedents in museum lighting studies and interactive media arts, but adapted to the specific conditions of our gallery space and equipment budget.

**8.1 Material Testing Protocol (Stream A)**

Each material sample will be mounted on a standardized frame (600 mm × 600 mm) positioned at a fixed distance of 2.4 m from the projector lens. The projection surface will be a matte white reference board for baseline calibration. For each of the 15 materials, we will record:

- Lux readings at 12 grid points using a calibrated lux meter (Konica Minolta CL-200A, on loan from the Department of Physics).
- Digital photographs at three exposure settings (0.3 EV under, correct, 0.3 EV over) to capture falloff characteristics.
- A written description of perceived texture, glare, and colour shift, completed by at least two independent observers.
- Ambient light readings before and after each session to control for variations in gallery daylight.

Testing will proceed in blocks of five materials per week, with projector warm-up and calibration checked at the start of each session. All data will be entered into the shared spreadsheet (link: drive/lumen-atelier/stream-A-log) and mirrored in the physical sample book.

**8.2 Spatial Prototyping Protocol (Stream B)**

Prototype construction will follow an iterative build-and-review cycle. Each prototype will be documented with:

- A floor plan sketch showing projector placement, viewing angles, and circulation paths.
- A lighting plan indicating expected lux distribution and any areas of concern.
- A log of visitor comments, transcribed from the comment cards at the end of each viewing week.

The three prototypes are designated P1 (corner projection), P2 (central island), and P3 (wall-mounted array). Each will occupy a distinct zone of BBG-2, and their placement will be adjusted according to the gallery's existing track lighting layout. Prototypes will remain in place for a minimum of three weeks each, with at least one week of overlap between successive installations to allow comparative viewing.

**8.3 Workshop and Exhibition Design (Stream C)**

The six workshops are designed for participants with no prior technical background. Each session will run for three hours on a Saturday morning, with a maximum of 12 participants. The workshop format will include:

- A 30-minute introduction to light as a material.
- A 90-minute hands-on session using portable projectors and a selection of test materials.
- A 30-minute group discussion and feedback form.

Workshop facilitators will be drawn from the project team, with assistance from two student volunteers from the School of Art, Design and Media (to be recruited in April 2025). The final exhibition will be curated by Dr. Raman, with installation support from the university's technical services team.

**9. Expected Outcomes**

The project will deliver:

1. **A material sample book** containing physical samples of all 15 diffusing materials, annotated with photometric data and qualitative observations. This will serve as a lasting reference for future lighting projects within the school.
2. **Three full-scale prototypes** installed in BBG-2, each demonstrating a different approach to projection in a shared gallery space.
3. **A white paper** summarising findings on material performance, spatial considerations, and visitor engagement. The white paper will be submitted to ORA alongside the final report, and will be made available on the school's research repository.
4. **A video documentation** looping during the exhibition, capturing the testing process, prototype construction, and selected workshop moments. This will be produced by a student videographer on a short-term contract.

documents.title: Lumen Atelier Project Proposal
documents.content:
The residency is organized around four primary objectives:

1. **Material Investigation:** To systematically test the optical behaviour of low-wattage LED projectors when directed through a range of diffusing materials (including frosted acrylic, woven polypropylene, and recycled paper pulp) under controlled ambient light conditions.
2. **Spatial Calibration:** To develop a repeatable methodology for mapping light projection zones within a 200-square-metre rectangular gallery space, accounting for ceiling height, wall reflectance, and floor surface variations.
3. **Public Engagement:** To conduct six weekend workshops for undergraduate students and the general public, during which participants will co-build small-scale light sculptures using the project's material library.
4. **Knowledge Dissemination:** To produce a technical white paper and a curated photographic archive documenting the project's processes, failures, and findings for use by peer institutions.

**4. Artistic Vision and Conceptual Framework**

Lumen Atelier operates from the premise that projected light, when treated as a sculptural material rather than a mere illuminant, can alter the perceived depth and weight of architectural surfaces. Our working methodology draws on the traditions of the Light and Space movement of the 1960s, but updates this lineage through the use of affordable, digitally controlled projection hardware. Rather than aiming for spectacle, the project seeks a quiet, almost forensic examination of how light falls, bends, and dissolves across everyday building materials.

The Black Box Gallery (BBG-2) presents a particularly interesting challenge: its walls are clad in a dark, low-reflectance microfibre fabric that absorbs most ambient light. This makes the space ideal for projection work but also means that our material tests must account for unusually high contrast ratios. We intend to treat this constraint as a generative condition, not a limitation.

**5. Research Methodology**

In the project proposal document, the Lumen Atelier project phase is listed as proposal. Record status: historical.

The project will proceed through three overlapping research streams:

- **Stream A – Material Testing (October – December 2024):** Systematic testing of 15 diffusing materials across 5 projector models. Each test will record lux readings at 12 fixed grid points, photographic documentation of light falloff, and qualitative notes on perceived texture. Data will be logged in a shared spreadsheet and a physical sample book.
- **Stream B – Spatial Prototyping (January – April 2025):** Construction of three full-scale prototype installations within BBG-2, each occupying a different zone of the gallery. Prototypes will be open for informal viewing by faculty and students, with visitor feedback collected via a simple comment card system.
- **Stream C – Public Workshops and Exhibition (May – September 2025):** Delivery of six workshops and the final exhibition, titled "Lumen Atelier: Provisional Findings." The exhibition will present the three prototypes in their final form, alongside the material sample book and a looped video documentation of the testing process.

**6. Proposed Timeline**

| Period | Activity | Milestone |
|--------|----------|-----------|
| Oct – Nov 2024 | Procurement of equipment and materials; calibration of testing protocol | Equipment inventory approved |
| Dec 2024 – Feb 2025 | Stream A: Material testing and data collection | Interim data report (internal) |
| Mar – Apr 2025 | Stream B: Prototype construction and informal viewing | Three prototypes installed |
| May 2025 | Workshop series begins (six sessions over six weekends) | First workshop delivered |
| Jun – Jul 2025 | Refinement of prototypes based on feedback; documentation of process | Documentation draft complete |
| Aug 2025 | Final exhibition installation | Exhibition opens |
| Sep 2025 | Exhibition closes; white paper drafting and submission of final report | Final report to ORA |

**7. Project Team**

**8. Methodology**

The project adopts a practice-based research methodology, combining quantitative photometric measurement with qualitative spatial observation. The approach is informed by precedents in museum lighting studies and interactive media arts, but adapted to the specific conditions of our gallery space and equipment budget.

**8.1 Material Testing Protocol (Stream A)**

Each material sample will be mounted on a standardized frame (600 mm × 600 mm) positioned at a fixed distance of 2.4 m from the projector lens. The projection surface will be a matte white reference board for baseline calibration. For each of the 15 materials, we will record:

- Lux readings at 12 grid points using a calibrated lux meter (Konica Minolta CL-200A, on loan from the Department of Physics).
- Digital photographs at three exposure settings (0.3 EV under, correct, 0.3 EV over) to capture falloff characteristics.
- A written description of perceived texture, glare, and colour shift, completed by at least two independent observers.
- Ambient light readings before and after each session to control for variations in gallery daylight.

Testing will proceed in blocks of five materials per week, with projector warm-up and calibration checked at the start of each session. All data will be entered into the shared spreadsheet (link: drive/lumen-atelier/stream-A-log) and mirrored in the physical sample book.

**8.2 Spatial Prototyping Protocol (Stream B)**

Prototype construction will follow an iterative build-and-review cycle. Each prototype will be documented with:

- A floor plan sketch showing projector placement, viewing angles, and circulation paths.
- A lighting plan indicating expected lux distribution and any areas of concern.
- A log of visitor comments, transcribed from the comment cards at the end of each viewing week.

The three prototypes are designated P1 (corner projection), P2 (central island), and P3 (wall-mounted array). Each will occupy a distinct zone of BBG-2, and their placement will be adjusted according to the gallery's existing track lighting layout. Prototypes will remain in place for a minimum of three weeks each, with at least one week of overlap between successive installations to allow comparative viewing.

**8.3 Workshop and Exhibition Design (Stream C)**

The six workshops are designed for participants with no prior technical background. Each session will run for three hours on a Saturday morning, with a maximum of 12 participants. The workshop format will include:

- A 30-minute introduction to light as a material.
- A 90-minute hands-on session using portable projectors and a selection of test materials.
- A 30-minute group discussion and feedback form.

Workshop facilitators will be drawn from the project team, with assistance from two student volunteers from the School of Art, Design and Media (to be recruited in April 2025). The final exhibition will be curated by Dr. Raman, with installation support from the university's technical services team.

**9. Expected Outcomes**

The project will deliver:

1. **A material sample book** containing physical samples of all 15 diffusing materials, annotated with photometric data and qualitative observations. This will serve as a lasting reference for future lighting projects within the school.
2. **Three full-scale prototypes** installed in BBG-2, each demonstrating a different approach to projection in a shared gallery space.
3. **A white paper** summarising findings on material performance, spatial considerations, and visitor engagement. The white paper will be submitted to ORA alongside the final report, and will be made available on the school's research repository.
4. **A video documentation** looping during the exhibition, capturing the testing process, prototype construction, and selected workshop moments. This will be produced by a student videographer on a short-term contract.

documents.content:
**2024-09-05 (Thu)**
Venue check. Called The Foundry admin. They confirmed the gallery is available for load-in from 15 Jan 2025. Exhibition opening can start 18 Jan 2025. No other bookings after that until mid-Feb. Good.

**2024-09-09 (Mon)**
Meeting with Dr. Raman to refine timeline. He wants a "soft open" for a small invited group on 17 Jan, but I noted that might complicate insurance. He said not critical.

**2024-09-12 (Thu)**
Draft budget submitted to Mei Ling. Key line items:
- LED modules and diffusers: $8,400
- Sound sensors and interface: $1,950
- Structural frame (aluminium): $2,700
- Lighting control system: $3,200
- Installation labour (2 students × 60 hrs @ $18): $2,160
- Transport and delivery: $450
- Contingency (5%): $1,000 approx.
Total ~$19,860. Mei Ling said CEMA cap is $20k, so we are within.

**2024-09-16 (Mon)**
Team meeting, 14:00. Dr. Raman showed updated sketches. The piece will have 12 suspended light "reeds" that sway and change colour based on sound input. He wants a test rig by end Oct.

**2024-09-20 (Fri)**
Ordered aluminium extrusion from AluPro (invoice #AP-2841). Estimated delivery 10 working days. Student assistants (Wei Jie and Priya) assigned to build test rig at the school workshop.

**2024-09-24 (Tue)**
Mei Ling flagged that CEMA requires a risk assessment for the installation, especially since it will be suspended from ceiling. I will draft and send to her by 30 Sep.

**2024-09-30 (Mon)**
Sent risk assessment draft to Mei Ling. Noted that the ceiling load at The Foundry is rated for 10 kg per point; our design uses 4 points, each ~8 kg max, so within limit. She said she will forward to CEMA for review.

---

**2024-10-02 (Wed)**
Aluminium arrived. Checked against invoice #AP-2841 — all 12 lengths present, no damage. Wei Jie started cutting.

**2024-10-07 (Mon)**
Test rig assembly begun at NUS workshop. Priya reported that the connectors from AluPro are slightly different from the spec sheet — they are 5mm shorter. I called AluPro; they said it's a batch change, should still work. Dr. Raman asked to see it by 15 Oct.

The project log records that The Foundry Art Space exhibition start date is 2025-01-18. Record status: current.

**2024-10-10 (Thu)**
Meeting with Dr. Raman, 15:30. He is happy with the rig progress. He wants to test the light response with a sample sensor. I ordered 2 sound sensors from Mouser (order #M-8821), expected 3–5 days.

**2024-10-15 (Tue)**
Test rig assembled. Wei Jie and Priya connected 4 LED modules. One module flickers; likely a loose solder joint. They will rework tomorrow.

**2024-10-17 (Thu)**
Sensors arrived. Tested one: it responds to claps but is too sensitive to ambient hum. Dr. Raman suggested a low-pass filter. I asked Wei Jie to check if the interface board supports that.

**2024-10-21 (Mon)**
Team meeting, 11:00. Dr. Raman was unwell, joined via video. Discussed the sensor issue. He wants a threshold adjustment. Wei Jie said he can modify the code in the Arduino interface. Mei Ling reminded that we need to submit a milestone report to CEMA by 1 Nov — mostly done, but she needs the test rig photos.

---

Year-end note from Dr. Raman: "Good progress this quarter. The piece is taking shape. Let us come back fresh in January and finish strong." I will add a summary to the project folder next week. documents.content:
# Lumen Atelier Project Log

**2025-01-10 (Fri)**
Wei Jie swapped the driver on LED module 3 this morning. Colour shift is resolved — all modules now read within ±50K of each other on the calibration meter. He also applied the 50 Hz notch filter to the far-end sensor feed. Priya did a quick A/B comparison in the lab; the HVAC hum is reduced by about 12 dB without affecting the upper frequencies. Dr. Raman approved the change.

Ms. Nurul confirmed the venue will be closed to the public on 11 Jan for final preparations. We have access from 08:00 to 20:00. The Foundry's technician will be on site from 09:00 to 17:00 if we need help with the 3-phase connection.

**2025-01-11 (Sat)**
Full installation day. Team arrived at 08:00. The Foundry's technician connected the 3-phase supply to the main rig. Wei Jie and Priya mounted the LED modules on the gallery's back wall. The sensor array was laid along the floor cable ramp, with the far-end sensor repositioned to avoid direct contact with the HVAC vent. Dr. Raman came by at 11:00 to review the layout. He asked for two small adjustments:
- Tilt the centre module slightly downward (about 5 degrees) to match the sightline from the main entrance.
- Move the backup recorder to the side alcove, away from the door, to reduce footfall noise during opening hours.

Both changes completed by 14:00. We ran a full system test at 15:00. All modules responded correctly; the sensor feed was clean. The backup recorder was set to start automatically at 10:00 daily.

One issue: the gallery's ceiling spotlight above the centre module is on a separate circuit that Ms. Nurul said will be switched off during daytime hours. We noted this in the setup sheet — it may affect the perceived brightness of the centre module. Dr. Raman said he will check during the opening.

**2025-01-12 (Sun)**
Installation complete. The project log records that The Lumen Atelier installation date is 2025-01-12. Record status: historical. This is the official date for the record; the venue opens to the public tomorrow.

Final checks this morning:
- All LED modules running at 80% brightness as per Dr. Raman's spec.
- Sensor array calibrated; no false triggers during a 30-minute walkthrough test.
- Backup recorder verified — it captured a clean 30-minute test clip.
- Insurance certificate displayed at the front desk (Mei Ling confirmed she sent the original to Ms. Nurul; a copy is in the project folder).

Dr. Raman sent a short note to the team at 16:00: "Thank you for the focused work this week. The piece is in place. Let us review the first day's feedback tomorrow."

- "The warm light at the centre is calming."
- "The hum is still there — is it intentional?" (This was from one visitor; the notch filter seems to have reduced it but not fully eliminated it in the centre area.)
- "The sensor response feels slow near the entrance."

We logged these in the visitor feedback sheet. Dr. Raman reviewed the comments and said the hum is acceptable as a "layer" (his earlier note). He asked us to note that the slow sensor response near the entrance is likely due to the distance from the main array; he will consider an additional sensor if it becomes a recurring comment.

**2025-01-15 (Wed)**
Mei Ling sent a reminder about the project budget review on 22 Jan. She attached a draft expenditure summary. I noticed the venue rental invoice from The Foundry was higher than the initial quote — Ms. Nurul explained it was due to the extra technician hours on 11 Jan. Mei Ling will follow up with the university's finance office to see if this can be absorbed under the contingency line.

Wei Jie started a maintenance log for the installation. He recorded the driver swap on 10 Jan and the notch filter adjustment. He also noted the spare driver and filter unit are stored in the lab storage room, labelled with the project name.

**2025-01-17 (Fri)**
Weekly check. Wei Jie ran a full diagnostic. All modules within spec. The backup recorder's SD card is at 60% capacity; he will swap it on 31 Jan. Priya reviewed the first week's sensor data — no anomalies.

documents.title: Lumen Atelier Project Log
documents.content:
One issue: the ceiling-mounted projector that had been used for the test loop on 14 Jan was borrowed from the AV office, and the AV office asked for it back by Monday. We returned it this evening. This means the small projection loop near the entrance will not run until we arrange a replacement. Dr. Raman said it is not critical; the piece works without it. Meeting at 10:00 in the CEMA office. Present: Ms. Nurul, Dr. Raman, Mei Ling, Priya. Wei Jie and I joined by video (we were on-site for a sensor check).

Key points:

- Total expenditure to date: S$38,240. Original approved budget: S$40,000. Remaining: S$1,760.

- Wei Jie to order the additional sensor (he has the part number from the earlier calibration).

Fine Arts confirmed they can lend us a projector for the run. Wei Jie picked it up this afternoon and set it up in place of the AV office unit. The projection loop is running again. Dr. Raman visited in the afternoon. He spent about 30 minutes in the space, observing visitor behaviour. She will continue to compile this weekly.

**2025-01-31 (Fri)**

- Monthly maintenance check done this morning. Wei Jie and I went through the sensor array and the projector. All readings within tolerance. - Facilities replied to Jason's email. They approved the extended hours for 28 Feb and 1 Mar, but noted that the building will be locked at 22:00 and the security guard will do a final round at 21:30. We need to ensure all visitors are out by 21:15.
